timeline.message:
Optimize BytesReferenceStreamInput Number Reads

`readByte` was used for all primitive reads which via the expensive `maybeNextSlice`
which did not inline well caused slowness when reading large aggregate messages.

This commit makes these reads do bulk operations on the underlying `byte[]` where possible
instead. Also, it extracts cold path from `maybeNextSlice` so that we get a fast bounds check
branch instead of the loop with a large body for the hot case.

closes #70800
timeline.author: Armin Braun

no need for double checking here, the slice lengths must be correct (it's an assumption we make in other places so the `maybeNextSlice` is all we need
Its worth leaving a comment here that we're being super intentional about moving the slow stuff to another method so the `if` statement is inlined.

This looks right to me. I think it's worth a jmh benchmark to prove to ourselves that we're really helping.

It isn't a "for now" thing, but I'd love to be able to assert that the jvm *can* inline methods we think are important to inline. We go to a lot of trouble to juggle things so the JVM can inline them but we don't have any way to test whether or not we've broken them. Some kind of test would be nice. But that ain't a "for now" thing.
